# MIT Department of Biological Engineering

> > The MIT Department of Biological Engineering advances biological engineering through research in synthetic biology, tissue engineering, microbiome science, and biomedical imaging, with strong ties to the Koch Institute, McGovern Institute, and MIT HEALS.

The department offers undergraduate (Course 20) and graduate programs focused on engineering living systems for applications in health, medicine, and biotechnology. Faculty and researchers collaborate across MIT's health and life sciences ecosystem, including the Broad Institute and Howard Hughes Medical Institute.

## Key Topics

- Biological Engineering
- Synthetic Biology
- Tissue Engineering
- Deep-tissue Imaging
- Microbiome Research
- Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research
- McGovern Institute for Brain Research
- MIT HEALS
- Nanoscale Imaging
- Epigenetics and Epitranscriptomics
- Spatial Biology
- Gene Expression Control
- Biomedical Sensors
- Organoid Development
- Immunology Tools

## Research News and Breakthroughs

- [High-Resolution Imaging More Accessible](https://be.mit.edu/about/news/a-new-method-makes-high-resolution-imaging-more-accessible): MIT researchers develop 20-fold tissue expansion for nanoscale imaging
- [Synthetic Gene Expression Control](https://be.mit.edu/about/news/a-new-system-can-dial-expression-of-synthetic-genes-up-or-down): MIT engineers create DIAL control system for synthetic gene expression
- [MRI Sensor for Brain Light Detection](https://be.mit.edu/about/news/new-sensor-uses-mri-to-detect-light-deep-in-the-brain): Alan Jasanoff's MRI sensor enables deep-tissue light detection for brain
- [Noninvasive Deep Tissue Imaging](https://be.mit.edu/about/news/noninvasive-imaging-method-can-penetrate-deeper-into-living-tissue): MIT develops label-free laser imaging for deeper tissue penetration
- [Engineered Bacteria Biosensors](https://be.mit.edu/about/news/engineered-bacteria-emit-signals-that-can-be-spotted-from-a-distance): Christopher Voigt's bacteria biosensors for remote agricultural monitoring
- [Game-Changing Immunology Tools](https://be.mit.edu/about/news/four-game-changing-immunology-tools-to-watch): Emerging immunology research techniques and single-cell analysis methods
- [Linda Griffith TIME100 Health Recognition](https://be.mit.edu/about/news/time100-health-linda-griffith-engineering-organs): Linda Griffith's tissue engineering work on endometriosis and organoids
